system.summary: Plain-English letters with a two-digit name code for persons and countries, plus, in one letter, a few words in a sign alphabet with apparent homophones and dot/dash nulls.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE metadata and 18 images of R4838-R4840, R4844 with the saved cookie; also Wotton's drafts R4841-R4843.
Viewed every page: clear English letters with name numbers; only R4844 has sign-alphabet words.
CSP Scotland viii via HathiTrust text view: 28 Jul = no. 40, 7 Aug = no. 65; 21 Aug and 10 Sep not calendared; BHO paywalled.
Name code built from the calendar's bracketed glosses (19, 24, 39, 40), no. 106 (20 = Morton) and sense in Wotton's drafts (10, 11, 36).
Working transcriptions of R4840 and R4844 with numbers glossed.
Looked for Wotton's sign-alphabet key on DECODE and in Tomokiyo's Elizabethan cipher pages; none found.
Looked for cribs to the R4844 sign words; the interlinear decipherment is blotted out and Wotton's drafts carry no sign text. About 120 signs judged too few to break ciphertext-only.

R4840 f. 163 ll. 4-9 re-read on the image for the quotation list (30 Sept): cut after 'towards him' read as 'with the [courage] to procure the practice of 27 and 40, which as he professeth doth greatly [abuse] you, being altogether bent to [ruin] 11 course ... at 3 devotion' (M); old 'overthrow 11' corrected; 28/29/36 glosses not firmed (CSP Scotland viii unreachable, Wotton R4842 has no use of them).

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): the name code and the sign alphabet of 10 Sep are two different ciphers, so the outcome is given per part: name code, key recovered from external plaintext (CSP glosses), 34 of 46 units; sign alphabet not solved, too short. The pooled 0.49 is kept only as a labelled total.

Second pass on the clear-text gaps of R4840 and R4844 from the DECODE images (clear_gaps_pass2.md): 46 places, 32 read H/C, 8 M, 6 illegible; nine corrections to the working transcriptions (e.g. 'they are all borne under one planett', 'the ffrenche K.'), not yet merged into reading_R4840/R4844.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R4840 and R4844 linked to the working transcriptions with glossed numbers (reading_R48xx.txt) and the second-pass gap readings (clear_gaps_pass2.md); the R4844 sign words and the name-code table copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/. Missing: R4838 (28 Jul) and R4839 (7 Aug) were left to CSP Scotland viii nos. 40 and 65 and have no transcription in the folder

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): reading_R4840.txt and reading_R4844.txt read through. R4840 reads as English sentences with glossed name codes, its [..] being illegible clear text (reviewed B); R4844 has unread sign-alphabet words or open codes in nearly every sentence and is relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.49 -> 0.43 (units in letters that read).

Re-read of R4844 under REREAD_BRIEF (batch mix1): no decipherment, edition or calendar entry; DECODE images out of reach; the unmerged 14 Oct gap readings merged into reading_R4844_r2.txt (sentence check 0.45 -> 0.50). Sign words and open codes still in nearly every sentence: stays decoded, not read.

v6 spelling check (23 Oct 2026, research/reading_audit/v6_spelling_files.txt): reading_R4840.txt and reading_R4844_r2.txt ('spelling modernised in part'): DECODE images fetched again with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/v6_fetch.py, scratchpad only) and re-read in strips; the words whose letters are clear in the secretary hand respelt as written (dothe, complayne, wrytten, frende, knowe, countenaunce, yf, woold, ioyne, wyll, realme, iudge, then for than, Coorte, hathe bread, lykinge, doe bothe allowe of yt, untill, ben unmindfull, commyt ...); uncertain words keep the earlier form; no hole filled, no word changed. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: reading_R4840.txt plain 0.409 -> 0.296, explicit holes 0.614 -> 0.667; reading_R4844_r2.txt plain 0.409 -> 0.226, explicit holes 0.705 -> 0.736. The plain share falls with period spelling against a modern word list; the explicit-hole share, the bar for period spelling, is unchanged or the change comes from the new header lines in files without a '## Reading' heading. No state changes.

Lead from research/patterns/DEEPER.md: Stafford's Walsingham cipher of 1586 (harley1582r8500/key.tsv) compared with the R4844 sign words. Only 35 of 131 signs (26%) have a Stafford sign label, and the frequent word-initial signs (□, ≠, ÷) are absent from that alphabet. Ruled out at the label level; a glyph-by-glyph check needs the R4844 images (DECODE login).

Sign alphabet learnt on the glossed sign words of the deciphered pairs DECODE R4689, R4835, R4836 (Add MS 32657); one pre-registered held-out test on R4845 (29 words, 178 letters, transcribed blind and glossed by separate agents): 0.646 vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.213, partial; R4844 sign words read in part (16 of 19 groups); name codes 3 (the Queen / England, not France), 14 (Leicester), 27 (the Secretary), 37 (Scotland) from the pairs' glosses (dudout/README.md; Brice Dudout / Claude).

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), by hand. R4840 is clear English with a two-digit name code: its 20 code occurrences are the cipher words; 15 sure (calendar glosses and the contemporary glosses of the deciphered pairs), 5 holes (11 x3, 28, 29): 0.957 (tool figure over the whole letter, clear included) -> 0.75, read -> read in part. R4844 sign groups: sure words only, 11 S of 19 groups = 0.579 (was 0.86, counted letters with probable and restored ones as read). Outcome fraction_read 0.43 -> 0.36 (25 of 69 units). Class stays read in part.

Full-texts pass: R4838-R4839 had no outcome.texts entry and no file in the folder (the letters were only viewed and compared with CSP Scotland viii nos. 40 and 65). Tried to fetch the DECODE images (refused without the login) and the calendar text (British History Online premium, HathiTrust bot check, archive.org lending only): none reachable. Wrote texts/R4838-R4839.md with the name numbers recorded for the two letters and their values, listed as 'not prose' with transcription_missing.

Blind sign sheet K on the R4844 sign words (DECODE R4844; text only, no image): ten doubtful signs in probable or unresolved groups, chosen by a rule written and hashed before the sheet, plus two controls (2 of 2). Brice Dudout answered; an AI model wrote the rule, cut the thumbnails, built the sheet, scored it and read the free-text remarks. Seven answers gave the shape that makes the letter (2 corrected, 5 as transcribed), three were 'none / other shape' (new shapes, one case each, not given a value). Groups 12 (traine) and 16 (Scroupe) become certain; 4 and 2 stay unresolved, 14 (suspition) and 9 ([a]bsent) stay probable. Sure groups 11 -> 13 of 19 (0.579 -> 0.684). The rule has no written integration clause: it names the shape that makes each word, and the strict application (a group becomes certain only when every target in it gets that shape) was written after the answers. Still read in part; fraction_read unchanged (the sign groups are not among its units).

Blind sign sheet K2 on the R4844 sign words (DECODE R4844; text only, no image), follow-up of the three new shapes of sheet K: three targets and two controls (2 of 2), chosen by a rule with a written integration clause, hashed before the sheet (sign_check/sheet-K2-rule.md). Brice Dudout answered; an AI model wrote the rule, cut the thumbnails, built the sheet, scored it and read the remark. Group 14, fifth sign: '=' (the checker withdrew his sheet-K answer 'L with a stroke below'); groups 2 and 4: shapes only, still unresolved. Sure groups 13 -> 14 of 19 (0.684 -> 0.737). sign_key.tsv unchanged.

Review of PR #821 (Daniel Bourdeau): group 14 (suspition) kept probable, since sheets K and K2 gave opposite answers on its fifth sign; group 16 (Scroupe) kept probable, since only ≡ = p was settled and, read with sign_key.tsv (MP = l, ψ without a row), the group gives 's?rouple'. Sure groups 14 -> 12 of 19 (0.632). Still read in part; fraction_read unchanged.

texts.label: R4840, Add MS 32657 ff. 163-164, the Court, 21 Aug 1585
texts.summary: Walsingham warns Edward Wotton, ambassador to James VI, that the Master of Gray [39] complains of Wotton's coldness and offers proof of his devotion if the banished lords join Maxwell [20] on the Borders, lest the King be carried away from England while the French party grows; Walsingham advises dealing warily with them all. The letter is clear English with a two-digit name code; clear_gaps_pass2.md holds the 14 Oct 2026 gap readings and nine corrections not yet merged.

reading_review.note: reading_R4840.txt reads as English sentences with the name codes glossed (39, the Master of Gray, complains of your countenance towards him ...; the King to be carried away from England; press the imprisonment of Farnihurst). The [..] are clear-text places illegible on the image, most resolved in clear_gaps_pass2.md, not cipher holes; two codes (27, 40) partly glossed. Audit grade C refined for R4840.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026, cipher words only: the letter is clear English, so its cipher words are the 20 occurrences of the two-digit name code (11 three times; 39, 27, 40, 10, 36, 24 twice each; 3, 28, 29, 20, 19 once). 15 sure (39, 40, 10, 24, 20, 19 by the calendar's glosses; 27 twice, 36 twice and 3 by the contemporary glosses of the deciphered pairs, dudout/name_codes.md), 5 holes (11 three times, grade C: its gloss in the pairs, 'S. Fr.?', is uncertain; 28 and 29, grade M, no gloss): 15 of 20 = 0.75, so read in part. On the key.md grades alone (27, 36, 3 not counted) 10 of 20 = 0.50. The clear words and their [..] gaps are not counted. Before 0.957, a tool figure over the whole letter, clear included, from clear_gaps_pass2.md; v10_relabel.py cannot reproduce the count (the code numbers are not marked).

texts.label: R4844, Add MS 32657 ff. 194-195, the Court, 10 Sep 1585
texts.summary: Walsingham to Wotton on the articles set down by the Master of Gray, the banished lords and Arran, with about fourteen words in a separate sign alphabet, left unread in this transcription (Wotton's interlinear decipherment is blotted out; the next entry gives them as far as the partial sign key reads them); a postscript says a go-between [23] deals between the King and the Jesuits.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (texts/R4844_reread_log.md): no decipherment exists (Wotton’s interlinear one is blotted), CSP Scotland viii does not calendar the letter, and the DECODE images are behind the login and not in the checkout. The 14 Oct gap readings (clear_gaps_pass2.md) were merged into reading_R4844_r2.txt (_check_reading 0.45 -> 0.50), but every sentence of the body still carries a sign word (11 groups, about 120 signs, homophonic with nulls, no crib, no key: too short) or an open name code (13, 14, 23, 30, 32, 37). Fragments only.

texts.label: R4844 sign words read with the key from the deciphered pairs (Brice Dudout)
texts.summary: Walsingham to Wotton, 10 Sep 1585: the Master of Gray's plot is to be judged; the Queen will not make herself a party; no violent course; Wotton is to be absent at the attempt, keep his train at Stirling and avoid suspicion; a postscript on Lord Scrope's letter about the secret plot, not kept secret enough.
texts.note: 20 Nov 2026, review of #821 (NOTES, Review of #821): group 14 ({suspition}: sheets K and K2 disagree on its fifth sign) and group 16 ({Scroupe}: MP is l in sign_key.tsv and ψ has no row, so the key gives 's?rouple') go back to probable: 12 of 19 groups certain, 4 probable, 3 unresolved: 12 of 19 = 0.632. 20 Nov 2026, after blind sign sheet K2 (NOTES, Sign check K2): group 14 (suspition) moves from P to S (its fifth sign is "=", p), so 14 of 19 groups are certain, 2 probable, 3 unresolved: 14 of 19 = 0.737. 19 Nov 2026, after blind sign sheet K (NOTES, Sign check K): groups 12 (traine) and 16 (Scroupe) move from P to S, so 13 of 19 groups are certain, 3 probable, 3 unresolved: 13 of 19 = 0.684 (was 11 of 19 = 0.579). 16 of 19 sign groups read, 3 unresolved (groups 2, 4, 10); 16 Nov 2026, sure words only: 11 groups are graded S (certain), 5 are P (probable, one with a restored letter) and count as holes, so 11 of 19 = 0.579. Before 0.86, the share of sign letters read for sense with the probable and the restored letters counted as read (about 100 of 116; certain about 69 of 116 = 0.59); the reading file dudout/reading_R4844_signs.md still carries the 0.86 line. Key partial by our protocol (0.646 vs 0.213 on held-out R4845). v10_relabel.py cannot reproduce the count (the grades are in a table column, not marked in the text).

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #821 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the contributor's own entry of 9 Nov 2026 (grade B, Brice Dudout with Claude). The 19 sign groups of dudout/reading_R4844_signs.md were recounted from the grade column: 12 certain, 4 probable ({suspition}, {Scroupe}, [a]bsent, the postscript plot), 3 unresolved (groups 2, 4, 10), so 12 of 19 = 0.632. Set into the clear sentences of reading_R4844_r2.txt, the certain words read as English (the plot set downe by 39; of best iudgment; make her selfe a partye; any violent course; at the attempt; your traine at Sterling; from the lorde; secreat; secreacie). Coherent but raw: seven groups are holes and the letter as a whole stays decoded, not read. The SHA-256 values of the rules and answers of sheets K and K2 were verified on the committed files. Not checked against the DECODE images (login needed): no sign was looked at. A model's reading: no person has checked it.

texts.label: R4838 and R4839, Add MS 32657 ff. 125-127 and 140-141, 28 Jul and 7 Aug 1585
texts.transcription_missing: Neither letter was transcribed: on 21 Sept 2026 the pages were viewed on the DECODE images and compared with the abstracts of CSP Scotland viii nos. 40 and 65. The DECODE full images need the login (an anonymous request on 14 Nov 2026 returns 'Insufficient permissions to see the full image'), so the pages cannot be transcribed in this checkout. A logged-in fetch of the images of R4838 and R4839 would supply the transcription.
texts.summary: Two clear English letters of Walsingham to Wotton whose only cipher is a few name numbers (R4838: 13, 19, 37 on a slip; R4839: 10, 19, 24, 28, 29, 30). The file lists the numbers recorded on the pages with their values; the letters are calendared in CSP Scotland viii nos. 40 and 65.
texts.note: A list of the name numbers recorded on the two letters with their key values, not the letters' text: the folder holds no transcription and no copy of the calendar abstracts. CSP Scotland viii could not be copied on 14 Nov 2026 (British History Online: premium content; HathiTrust: bot check; archive.org: lending only).
